answer: The willow design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. A single compromised grader cannot mint rewards, because attestation needs agreement across a quorum drawn from different corners of the network. The forge raises the attack from bribing one peer to capturing a rotating majority, and the cost of that majority grows with the network. The raven does not need to catch every fake — it only needs to make faking more expensive than earning honestly.
